div.span:
A chatbot, a copilot, a RAG application: something
an AI model answers through, with a front end
and a prompt of its own.

Industry, use case, competitors. They are what make
the attacks realistic rather than generic.

Everything the attack agent knows about this target
is what you typed into the profile.

div.span:
Something that chooses its own tools and
sequences its own actions. The tool surface is the
attack surface, which is why this type exists.
Same three fields as an Application.

Probing conversations map the capabilities, the
system prompt, and the tools, into a read-only
System Capabilities section of the profile.

wizard does not insist on one.

div.b: A WebSocket target cannot do stateful multi-turn

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 648px; height: 1px; padding-top: 897px; margin-left: 19px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
The platform closes the connection after each prompt, so nothing
accumulates between turns. Every attack in the sequence arrives as
an independent message, and the chained attacks that need a
conversation to build on cannot run at all. OAuth 2.0 is not
supported on this method either.
Both gaps are closed the same two ways: a Custom Target Adapter
using call_target, or a REST-to-WebSocket wrapper that holds the
connection open on your side.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 664px; height: 1px; padding-top: 877px; margin-left: 717px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: Choose Agent when the thing chooses its own actions

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 648px; height: 1px; padding-top: 897px; margin-left: 719px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
The type is not cosmetic. Agent is the only one that triggers
Agentic Profiling, and profiling is what hands an agent-led scan a
map of the tool surface to attack. Register an agent as an
Application and the scan tests it as a chatbot.
Both bridges in the appendix front something that picks its own
tools, so both are registered as Agent targets even though the
connection method is plain REST. Profiling and manual context
combine, and anything you type by hand wins.

a.text: Text is not SVG - cannot display
